part.text:
All tests pass. The fix is a single change in `specs_setter::on_zero` (include/fmt/core.h:2239): previously it rewrote the fill character to `'0'` even when an explicit alignment (`<`, `>`, `^`) had already been parsed, so `"{:<06}"` produced `-42000` instead of `-42   `. Now `'0'` is ignored whenever an align option is set, matching the standard; it still sets `align::numeric` with a `'0'` fill when no alignment was given (`"{:06}"` → `-00042` still works).

Verification:
- `format_test.zero_flag_and_align` (the FAIL_TO_PASS case) passes, along with the full `format-test`, `core-test`, `printf-test`, `xchar-test`, `chrono-test`, `compile-test`, and all other suites.
- Issue examples verified: `{:<06}` → `-42   `, `{:>06}` → `   -42`, plus `^` and explicit-fill variants behave correctly.
